subject: Post-call: performance checkpoints & customer k6 scripts
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Sutherland <maya@bluefin.ai>, Mike Chen <mike.chen@bluefin.ai>, Tara Singh <tara@bluefin.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: performance checkpoints & customer k6 scripts

Hi Maya / Mike / Tara —

Great call earlier, thanks for walking through the traffic profile. Quick recap and the concrete next steps we agreed on so nothing slips: 

High-level SLO targets (agreed):
- P95 latency (generation, 256 tokens): < 350ms
- Sustained throughput: 120 req/s for the test window
- Peak concurrency (streaming clients): 40 concurrent streaming sessions
- Minimal cold-start impact via warmed KV cache for prefix-heavy traffic

Customer-led load test plan & logistics:
- You (Bluefin) will provide the k6 scripts and test matrices (percentile/input size variants) — we expect those by EOD Thu (2027-06-17).
- Test window we tentatively scheduled: 2027-06-22 02:00–04:00 UTC (we can shift +/- 1 hour if needed).
- Bluefin to supply the source IP ranges that need to be allowlisted for the runs (include CIDR if possible).
- Redwood will provision a reserved test pool and create short-lived API keys for the run (read below for names).

Action items (owners):
- [Bluefin] Attach k6 scripts + test matrix (Maya) — due 2027-06-17 EOD.
- [Bluefin] Provide source IPs for allowlist (Mike) — due 2027-06-17 EOD.
- [Redwood] Create test API key and service account: bluefin-test-2027-06 (Dylan) — target 2027-06-18 morning PT.
- [Redwood-SE] Validate model variant and runtime profile, pre-warm KV cache and provide runbook (Marissa) — target 2027-06-18.
- [Both] Final confirmation of test window and runbook by 2027-06-18 EOD.

Attachments I've added for reference: redwood-slo-template.xlsx (SLO definitions we use), a short runbook excerpt describing cache warm path and streaming toggles. If you attach the k6 tarball please include any secrets config (placeholder values are fine).

Questions / constraints we flagged on the call:
- If scripts open a very large number of long-lived streaming connections we may need to temporarily increase per-customer connection quotas — we'll flag if that's required but want to try with current caps first.
- Please include a small representative dataset (<= 10K tokens) in the test matrix so we can validate sequence-length tail behavior.

Thanks — will follow up with the test key and allowlist instructions once I create them.

Best,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-slo-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), runbook-excerpt.md (text)

Thanks Dylan — that layout looks right. We're attaching the initial k6 bundle and the test matrix. Quick notes from our side: 

- Attached: bluefin-k6-scripts-v1.tar.gz (includes v1 script, env.example, and README with session durations).
- Test matrix in the spreadsheet includes three bands: light (40 RPS), nominal (120 RPS), heavy (200 RPS). For the official SLO run we plan to execute the nominal band (120 RPS).
- IP ranges for our cloud agents: 35.198.12.0/22, 34.72.88.0/23 — please confirm allowlist acceptance.
- We'll point the scripts at the test key you create; if you can generate one that limits usage to the test window that would be ideal.

Mike (copied) will coordinate on the IP list and can be primary SRE contact during the run.

Maya Sutherland
Director, Platform Engineering
Bluefin Analytics

Copying down our internal checklist for the run so ops has a single source of truth. I'm adding estimated durations for each prep task.

Redwood prep checklist (internal):
- Create scoped test API key (bluefin-test-2027-06) + log retention flag = 30d — Dylan (30 min)
- Reserve dedicated inference pool (2x medium-quant nodes) for 2 hours around test window — Infra (1 hr)
- Configure IP allowlist for test key: 35.198.12.0/22, 34.72.88.0/23 — Dylan (15 min)
- Pre-warm KV cache with representative prefixes (run small warm job) — Marissa (45 min)
- Validate streaming concurrency settings, increase if we see connection throttles — Marissa / Infra (30 min)
- Smoke run with a subset (10 RPS) 24 hours before main window — schedule for 2027-06-21 02:00–02:15 UTC — Neha to confirm with Bluefin

Notes and model guidance:
- Use model variant rwdx-medium-quant for parity with production latency targets. We'll document any quantization artifacts in the runbook.
- If heavy memory pressure appears we have a fallback policy to move to rwdx-large-quant but that may change latency.

I'll produce the mini-run runbook and post it to the shared Drive link. Neha, please confirm the smoke-run schedule with Bluefin and I'll start the infra reservations once Dylan confirms the key name.

-Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>

Thanks all — quick confirmations and what I've done: 

- Created API key: bluefin-test-2027-06 (scoped to inference and active window). I'll DM the key to Maya and Mike; it will expire 2027-06-23 08:00 UTC.
- IP allowlist entries created for the key: 35.198.12.0/22, 34.72.88.0/23 — please verify connectivity from your agents.
- Reserved a small dedicated pool for the window (2 rwdx-medium-quant nodes) and queued the pre-warm job (will run once you confirm the smoke window).

Next steps for Bluefin: please run the small smoke (10 RPS) on 2027-06-21 02:00–02:15 UTC and share the run log so we can validate warm cache behavior. For the main run (2027-06-22 02:00–04:00 UTC) we'll monitor token-level latency and stream depth.

If anything changes to the script (for example very long streaming heartbeats) call it out in the README — those are the sorts of cases where we may need a short quota bump temporarily.

I'll upload the runbook excerpt and the SLO spreadsheet to the Drive and attach here.

Best,
Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
